sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 79. Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object in any form, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine

learningObjectives: Understand verbal and gestural insult to modesty under BNS s. 79.
Analyze the three modes: uttering words/sounds, making gestures/exhibiting objects, and intruding upon privacy.
Examine the statutory penalty: simple imprisonment up to three years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 79 provides that whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A woman's modesty can be outraged through speech, sound, indecent gestures, visual display of obscenity, or unwarranted intrusions upon her private domain, even without physical contact.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 79 (corresponding to IPC s. 509).
Actor: 'Whoever' (gender-neutral: can be committed by a man or woman).
Mode 1: Uttering any word or making any sound intending it to be heard by the woman.
Mode 2: Making any gesture or exhibiting any object intending it to be seen by the woman.
Mode 3: Intruding upon the privacy of such woman.
Mens rea: 'intending to insult the modesty of any woman'.
Penalty: Simple imprisonment up to three years, and with fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused uttered a word/sound, made a gesture, exhibited an object, or intruded upon privacy.
The word/sound was intended to be heard, or gesture/object was intended to be seen by the woman.
The act was done with the specific intention of insulting the modesty of that woman.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 79 is the non-contact verbal and gestural modesty provision (traditionally known as street harassment or eve-teasing). Unlike Section 74 which requires an assault or physical force, Section 79 operates entirely in the verbal, auditory, visual, and spatial realm. Catcalling, making obscene sexual gestures with hands, singing lewd songs directed at a passing woman, exhibiting obscene items or adult toys in her sight to humiliate her, or peeping into her private room constitutes an offence under s. 79. The BNS prescribes simple imprisonment up to three years and fine.
examples: Teaching example (Lewd street remarks): An accused stands outside a women's college gate and repeatedly shouts obscene, sexually derogatory comments at passing students. Section 79 applies directly; he faces up to three years imprisonment.

Teaching example (Obscene gesture): A driver cuts off a female driver at an intersection, rolls down his window, and makes explicitly obscene sexual hand gestures directed at her. Section 79 is violated.
distinctions: Section 74 (Physical force) vs Section 79 (Verbal/Gesture): Section 74 requires physical assault; Section 79 penalizes words, sounds, gestures, and privacy intrusion without physical touch.

Section 75(iv) (Sexually coloured remarks) vs Section 79 (Insulting modesty): Section 75(iv) can only be committed by a man against a woman; Section 79 uses 'whoever' and applies to any person insulting a woman's modesty.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an individual who placed an obscene drawing under the door of a female neighbor with her name written on it is liable under BNS s. 79.
Rule: Section 79 penalizes exhibiting any object or uttering words intending to insult the modesty of a woman.
Application: The drawing was explicit, targeted, and placed intentionally to be seen by her, with intent to insult her modesty.
Conclusion: The individual is guilty under s. 79.
